macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. markets set for a quiet open as investors wait for Fed signals
items.summary: U.S. stock-index futures were little changed as investors looked ahead to Federal Reserve guidance on interest rates, with Wall Street broadly focused on the next policy move. Market commentary says traders currently expect the Fed to hold rates steady next month.

items.title: Futures and rates markets still centered on the Fed’s next step
items.summary: Recent market coverage says Wall Street expects the Federal Reserve to keep rates unchanged at the next meeting, reinforcing a wait-and-see tone across stocks and bonds. The key macro theme remains how long policy will stay restrictive if inflation and growth data remain mixed.

items.title: Major U.S. inflation data eased, supporting a softer rate-cut outlook
items.summary: Recent economic coverage reported that U.S. inflation cooled to 3.4% in July, down from the prior month, with food costs slowing and energy prices helping to ease headline pressure. That trend has helped keep expectations alive for eventual policy easing, even as the timing remains uncertain.

items.title: Wall Street markets remained near record levels amid resilience in growth and earnings
items.summary: Market commentary indicated U.S. stocks had recently rallied to all-time highs, with the S&P 500 setting both intraday and closing records. The move has been supported by strong earnings growth and a still-resilient economy.

items.title: Labor market data stayed firm despite some cooling in hiring and claims
items.summary: Recent U.S. labor-market indicators showed unemployment claims edging higher while layoffs stayed historically low, pointing to ongoing labor resilience. Separate commentary noted hiring has slowed versus prior years, but overall job security remains unusually strong.

items.title: Housing remains a key macro focus as mortgage rates drift lower
items.summary: Recent housing data showed existing-home sales falling in July, even as mortgage rates ticked slightly lower. Analysts are watching whether lower borrowing costs and better inventory can support a late-year rebound in housing activity.

items.title: India macro watch: RBI steady rates, crude imports surge, and equities consolidate
items.summary: Indian market coverage highlighted the Reserve Bank of India keeping rates steady, record Russian crude imports in July, and expectations for range-bound trading as investors watch oil prices and global central-bank signals. Domestic market participants are also focused on upcoming macro releases and FOMC minutes.

items.title: This week’s market agenda centers on retail earnings and Fed minutes
items.summary: Market previews say investors will be watching FOMC minutes, housing data, and retail-sector earnings for clues on consumer demand and policy direction. The calendar also includes regional manufacturing indicators and broader PMI releases.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin trades above $63,000 as crypto market mostly mixed
items.summary: Bitcoin was trading above $63,000 with a slight 24-hour gain, while Ether, XRP, Solana, BNB, Cardano, Dogecoin, and TRUMP showed mixed performance. The report also noted that Binance will restrict transactions involving HTX and 10 other crypto platforms for UK and EU users from August 23.

items.title: Polymarket says it is refunding some users after a frontend compromise
items.summary: Polymarket said a third-party vendor had been compromised and a malicious script was injected into its frontend for some users, prompting refunds for affected accounts. The incident highlights ongoing security risks across crypto platforms.

items.title: Portugal orders Polymarket to shut down
items.summary: Portuguese regulators gave Polymarket 48 hours to cease operations after users wagered more than 103 million euros on the platform. The order adds to growing regulatory scrutiny of prediction markets and crypto-linked betting services.

items.title: Fidelity is reportedly launching its own stablecoin
items.summary: A report cited by The Verge says Fidelity is preparing to launch its own stablecoin, signaling continued expansion by major financial firms into digital assets. The development would further blur the line between traditional finance and crypto-native payment rails.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches faster GPT-5.6 'Ultrafast' mode
items.summary: OpenAI has introduced a preview of 'Ultrafast,' a speed-optimized mode for GPT-5.6 Sol that the company says runs 14 times faster, with the move aimed at enterprise users who need lower latency. The announcement adds to a wave of rapid model iterations among frontier AI labs.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 3.7 Flash
items.summary: Google announced Gemini 3.7 Flash just three weeks after Gemini 3.6 Flash, signaling a very fast release cadence and what the company describes as substantial improvements. The update highlights continued competition in lightweight, high-throughput AI models.

items.title: Meta launches a new AI model to push its open-source strategy
items.summary: Meta released a new artificial intelligence model and framed it as part of its effort to build the best open-source model and compete more effectively with Chinese rivals. The announcement underscores the growing strategic importance of open models in the AI race.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic intensify price competition as Chinese rivals gain ground
items.summary: Industry coverage notes a price war between OpenAI and Anthropic as both US firms respond to mounting pressure from lower-cost Chinese AI models. The trend suggests that pricing, not just capability, is becoming a central battleground in frontier AI.

items.title: Anthropic adds watermarking to AI-generated content
items.summary: Anthropic is reportedly introducing watermarks for AI-generated content, with coverage saying the change is intended to support EU compliance efforts. The move reflects broader industry pressure for provenance and transparency tools.

items.title: Flock adds safeguards to AI surveillance tools after backlash
items.summary: Flock is rolling out new safety controls for its AI surveillance products after criticism over misuse and privacy concerns. The update shows how regulatory and public scrutiny is shaping deployment of AI in law enforcement.

items.title: Hackers used AI in an autonomous attack on Taiwan government agencies
items.summary: CNN reports that hackers deployed an AI system in what experts believe was the first known fully autonomous cyberattack against government agencies in Taiwan. The incident is a notable escalation in the use of AI for offensive cyber operations.

items.title: Stripe reportedly to acquire AI gateway startup OpenRouter for more than $7B
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that Stripe is in line to acquire AI gateway startup OpenRouter in a deal reportedly valued at over $7 billion. If completed, the acquisition would be one of the biggest AI infrastructure deals to date.

items.title: SpaceX officially closes its Cursor acquisition
items.summary: TechCrunch says Cursor, the AI coding startup, is now officially part of SpaceX. The deal adds another sign that major tech and industrial firms are continuing to buy AI tools and talent.
